h: Pairing the Weird With the Wonderful
p: Ripley's makes a great short stop rather than an all-day affair, which means it slots neatly into a bigger Blackpool itinerary. Families often use it as a breather between the bigger rides, or as a rainy-afternoon plan when the beach is out of the question. You can usually see the whole thing in an hour or two at a relaxed pace, though curious kids who stop to read every sign will happily take longer.

Turn the visit into a game. Before you go in, ask everyone to guess the weirdest thing they'll see, then compare notes at the end. Get the kids to pick their favourite exhibit and their most disgusting one, which they will absolutely enjoy doing. Older children might like to keep a list of the most mind-boggling facts to amaze their mates with back at school.

Illusions and interactive bits make for brilliant photos, so keep your phone handy and be ready to pose. A few exhibits might be a touch unnerving for the very young, so it's worth staying close and steering around anything that looks like it might cause nightmares.

If the weather stays grim, Blackpool has plenty more under cover. Sandcastle Waterpark, right by the Pleasure Beach, is a big indoor water park with slides and pools for all ages. Further up the prom, the Blackpool Tower complex houses the famous Tower Ballroom, with its Wurlitzer organ and gilded ceiling, as well as the Tower Eye viewing platform. The Winter Gardens, a grand Victorian entertainment venue in the town centre, is worth a look for its architecture alone.
